story-12-purpose-aristotle.label: Purpose
lines: “All men by nature desire to know.”
Learn one thing today that nobody is paying you to learn. That hunger is the start of a purpose.

story-13-suffering-marcus.label: Suffering
lines: “Everything that happens is either endurable or not. If it’s endurable, then endure it. Stop complaining.”
Harsh, and he wrote it to himself. Most of what you’re carrying tonight is endurable. Carry it to bed and sleep.
story-13-suffering-marcus.footer: Screenshot this for a heavy night.

story-14-virtue-plato.label: Virtue
lines: “Wealth does not bring about excellence, but excellence makes wealth and everything else good for men.”
Socrates, on trial for his life. Get good first. The rest follows, and it’s safe in your hands when it does.

story-15-amorfati-marcus.label: Amor fati
lines: “All that is in tune with you, O Universe, is in tune with me.”
Not resignation. Agreement. Tonight, say yes to one thing you didn’t choose.

story-16-purpose-seneca.label: Purpose
lines: “Philosophy moulds and constructs the soul; it orders our life, guides our conduct, shows us what we should do and what we should leave undone.”
This isn’t a hobby. It’s a map. Read one page of Marcus or Epictetus before you open any app today.

story-17-beauty-marcus.label: Beauty
lines: “Even the by-products of nature have a grace and charm of their own.”
He meant bread cracking open in the oven, figs bursting, a lion’s heavy brow. Look at one ordinary thing tonight until it becomes beautiful.

story-18-suffering-frankl.label: Suffering
lines: “When we are no longer able to change a situation, we are challenged to change ourselves.”
Viktor Frankl, Man’s Search for Meaning
Some things won’t move. The job, the diagnosis, the past. Then the work moves inside you. That’s not defeat. That’s the assignment.

story-19-virtue-epictetus.label: Virtue
lines: “Be silent for the most part, or speak only what is necessary.”
Try it for one evening. Say less, listen more, and notice how much stronger you feel by the end.

story-20-amorfati-marcus.label: Amor fati
lines: “Whatever happens to you has been waiting to happen since the beginning of time.”
Friday. Whatever today brings was always going to be yours. Meet it like you were expecting it.

story-21-beauty-nietzsche.label: Beauty
lines: “Without music, life would be a mistake.”
Friedrich Nietzsche, Twilight of the Idols
The man who wrote about suffering also wrote this. Put on the one song that makes you feel alive and play it loud tonight.

story-22-virtue-marcus.label: Virtue
lines: “Injustice is often done by not doing.”
Standing by is a choice. The friend who needs a call, the wrong you saw and ignored. Being a good man includes the things you didn’t do.

story-23-purpose-marcus.label: Purpose
lines: “Concentrate every minute on doing what’s in front of you with precise and genuine seriousness.”
Saturday night. Purpose isn’t one big thing you find. It’s the next thing in front of you, done properly.

story-24-amorfati-marcus.label: Amor fati
lines: “To love only what happens, what was destined. No greater harmony.”
Sunday morning. Look back at the week and find one thing that went wrong that you can now be glad about.

story-25-beauty-epictetus.label: Beauty
lines: “What else can I do, a lame old man, but sing hymns to God?”
A former slave with a broken leg, teaching in exile, choosing gratitude. If he could sing, you can say thank you for one thing tonight.

panels: Me: *loses one argument with a stranger online*
*thinks about the perfect comeback for three days*
“Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views which they take of things.”

carousel-8.label: For young men
lines: 5 ancient lines for when life gets heavy.
“I judge you unfortunate because you have never been unfortunate. You have passed through life without an adversary; no one will know what you were capable of, not even you.”
The easy life never finds out who you are.
“Nothing happens to anyone that he can’t endure.”
Others have carried this exact weight. You can too.
“What would Hercules have been if there had been no lion, hydra, stag or boar?”
No monsters, no hero. Your problems are the plot.
“What does not kill me makes me stronger.”
Friedrich Nietzsche, Twilight of the Idols
Overused because it’s true. But only if you let it work on you.
“What is to give light must endure burning.”
The men who light the way for others have all been through the fire.

carousel-14.label: Your turn
lines: Which one do you need this week?
Save this. Send it to a brother who’s going through it.
